Alternatively, from Proto-Semitic *libb- (“heart”), with the initial ق possibly being a phonological insertion to break a biconsonantal cluster and avoid *∅alb or *∅ulb, thus *lb → *∅alb → qalb. See also Arabic لُبّ (lubb), "core, heart, intellect", without q
From Proto-Semitic *qayθ̣- (“summer”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *ḳayč̣- (“to be hot; summer”). Cognate with Aramaic קֵיטָא (qēṭā) and Hebrew קַיִץ (káyits, qáyiṣ).

From the root ل ف ت (l f t) in the sense of twisting or wringing out of the ground, "to pull up or extract". Ultimately, from Proto-Semitic *lapt-. Compare: Hebrew לֶפֶת (lefet, “turnip”), Classical Syriac ܠܰܦܬܳܐ (laftā, “turnip”), Akkadian 𒇻𒂠𒊬 (LU.UB₂.SAR /⁠laptu, liptu⁠/, “turnip”).
From Proto-Semitic *lawn, from Proto-Afroasiatic *lwn-; cognate with Egyptian jwn.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *laylay-.

From Proto-Semitic *mawut-. Cognate with Hebrew מֵת (mét), Aramaic מית (mīt), Tigrinya ሞተ (motä), Egyptian mwt. False cognate of Malay and Indonesian mati and all its Austronesian cognates.
Noun of place from a noun designating “urine” descending from Proto-Semitic *ṯayn- f (“urine”) which has not found in the records of the Arabic language before being ousted by بَوْل (bawl, “urine”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *muḫḫ- (“head; brain; marrow”).

parole.significato: thick mud; clayey and loamy earth

From Proto-Semitic *maraṣ̂- (“to be ill”). Compare Akkadian 𒍼 (marāṣum, “to be ill, diseased”), Biblical Hebrew נִמְרַץ (nimraṣ, “to be sore”) and Ugaritic 𐎎𐎗𐎕 (mrṣ).
From Proto-Semitic *mušy-; synchronically, from the root م س ي (m s y).

parole.significato: to stroke with the hand or similar, to wipe off, to sweep
parole.testo: Compare Ugaritic 𐎎𐎌𐎈 (mšḥ) and Hebrew מָשַׁח (mašáḥ, “to anoint”).

From Proto-Semitic *śaʕr- (“hair”).

parole.significato: to carve (wood or stone), to sculpt, to shave, to plane, to smooth, to scratch, to saw off, to excavate (a rock)

Inherited from Proto-Semitic *niḥnu. Cognate with Hebrew אנחנו.

parole.significato: to emit a sound through the nose, to snort, to grunt
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *naḫar-. In Arabic compare خَرْخَرَ (ḵarḵara, “to snore”), نَعَرَ (naʕara), نَعَقَ (naʕaqa).

parole.significato: to be raised, to be lifted, to rise up
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *naśaʔ- (“lift, raise”). Compare Ge'ez ነሥአ (näśʾä, “to lift, to take”), Akkadian 𒈾𒋗𒌑𒌝 (našûm) and Biblical Hebrew נָשָׂא (nɔśɔʾ).
From the root ن ف خ (n f ḵ), the verb from Proto-Semitic *napaḫ-. Compare also Arabic نَفَحَ (nafaḥa, “to spread, to diffuse; to blow”).

parole.significato: To cease to exist, to vanish from being, to perish

Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šum.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šuʔa.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šiʔa.

parole.significato: and, a divider of words or clauses, particle of connection or continuation often unnecessary to render in translation,…
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *wa. Cognate with Hebrew וְ־ (wə-).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔaḥad- ~ *waḥad- (“one”).

parole.significato: to carry much rain, to rain violently, heavily

From Proto-Semitic *waqar- (“to be heavy or weighty; a tree laden with fruits; to be honorable or to hold weight in value”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *waqar-; compare Egyptian jqr (“excellent, worthy”) and Hebrew יָקָר (“expensive, dear, precious”).

From Proto-Semitic *-ay-.

From Proto-Semitic *yamīn- (“right”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *yamin- (“right”).
From Proto-Semitic *nabaʕ- (“to flow”).
